To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
overexpression of IGFBP- 1 in fetal hepatocytes is sufficient to cause Fetal Growth Restriction.
overexpression of IGFBP- 1 in the fetal liver is sufficient to cause Fetal growth restriction (Fgr).
elevated circulating IGFBP1 is sufficient to induce FGR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of insulin-like growth factors (IGFs) and their binding proteins (IGFBPs) in fetal growth.
understanding the role of IGF binding proteins (IGFBP) in regulating fetal growth.
the role of IGF binding protein (BP)-1 in regulating fetal growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
high levels of circulating IGFBPs can cause FGR.
the elevated circulating IGFBP1 in the AFP-BP transgenic mice was responsible for the FGR phenotype.
elevated circulating IGFBP-I is sufficient to cause Fetal growth restriction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high levels of circulating IGFBPs are sufficient to cause IGF-dependent fetal growth restriction.
elevated circulating IGFBP1 is sufficient to produce fetal growth restriction (IGF-BP1 is an IGF inhibitor).
the placenta is the key regulator of the IGF axis in the fetus, and that high circulating IGFBPs can override this regulatory mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
elevated IGFBP- 1 is sufficient to induce FGR in the mouse.
the IGF system is a critical regulator of placental and fetal development and that high concentrations of IGFBP-4 and/or IGFBP-5 in the placenta are sufficient to cause IUGR in mice.
high circulating levels of IGF binding protein 1 (IGFB1) cause fetal growth restriction (fGR) in mice.
